Recovery Service What's Included in Vehicle Recovery Professional flatbed recovery - safe transport for your vehicle. ✅ What's Included 🛻 Flatbed recovery Professional flatbed truck - safe transport (not tow rope). ⬆️ Vehicle loading Professional loading onto the flatbed. 🔒 Vehicle securing Proper strapping and securing for transport. 🏁 Transport to workshop Delivery to your chosen workshop. ⬇️ Vehicle unloading Professional unloading at the workshop. 📋 Basic assessment On-arrival assessment of vehicle condition. ⚠️ What's NOT Included Towing Tow ropes can damage vehicles - we only recommend flatbed recovery. Why Flatbed Flatbed Recovery - Why It's the Right Choice Not all recovery methods are equal. Here's why flatbed is the only safe option for engine and gearbox failures. 🛻 Flatbed Recovery ✅ Safe - Minimal risk to vehicle Vehicle fully secured - all wheels off the ground Best for: All vehicles - especially those with engine/gearbox failure 🔗 Tow Rope ❌ Not safe - High risk Can damage suspension, gearbox, bodywork Best for: Emergency only - not recommended 🔧 Tow Bar / A-Frame ⚠️ Partial - Medium risk Can damage gearbox in automatics Best for: Only if vehicle is drivable and follows regulations 🛞 Dolly Towing ⚠️ Partial - Medium risk Can damage gearbox Best for: Specialist only No gearbox damage All wheels are off the ground - no strain on transmission. No suspension damage Vehicle is fully supported - no bouncing or stress. Safe for automatics No risk of transmission damage from towing. Safe for low-profile vehicles No risk of scraping or bottoming out. Professional loading Vehicle is properly secured - no movement during transport. "We always recommend flatbed recovery for engine and gearbox failures. If you tow a vehicle with a snapped timing chain on an automatic gearbox, you can destroy both the engine AND the gearbox. The extra £50-£100 for a flatbed is cheap insurance." - UK Recovery Specialist Interview #3 [EM-INTERVIEW] · (names withheld at specialist's request) Supply and Fit + Recovery Recovery + Engine Replacement - Combined Service Many of our specialists can provide a combined service, saving you time and coordination. 🚛 Vehicle recovery Flatbed recovery from your location to the workshop 🔧 Engine supply Used, reconditioned, rebuilt, or new - you choose 🔩 Engine fitting Professional installation at the workshop 🛡️ Warranty Varies by condition type and supplier 🧪 Testing Post-installation testing - oil pressure, compression, leaks The Benefit of Combined Service Separate Services You coordinate recovery + engine supplier + fitter · Timing may not align · Potentially higher cost · Multiple parties to coordinate Combined Service One contact - all arranged · Recovery scheduled around workshop availability · Often lower cost - combined quote · One party responsible for the whole job Get combined recovery + engine replacement quotes → Get Combined Quotes Checklist Recovery Checklist - What to Do Before Collection A step-by-step guide to prepare your vehicle for recovery. Before the Recovery Vehicle Arrives 1 Remove personal items Empty the vehicle of all personal belongings - they may be lost or damaged during transport. 2 Remove toll passes / tickets Remove any parking permits, toll tags, or passes - they may not be returned. 3 Check vehicle is clear Ensure the vehicle is accessible - clear any obstructions for safe loading. 4 Release handbrake If safe to do so - for loading purposes, the driver may need to move the vehicle. 5 Note fuel level Record the current fuel level for your records - in case the workshop needs to move it. 6 Check for damage Walk around the vehicle - take photographs of any existing damage for your records. 7 Photograph the vehicle Take clear photos of all four sides and the interior - evidence of condition before transport. 8 Have keys ready Have all keys ready for the driver - they need to move the vehicle onto the flatbed. During the Collection 1 Ask for the driver's ID Ask for the driver's ID or company identification - verify they are from the recovery company you booked. 2 Ask about any images taken Ask the driver if they have taken photos of the vehicle for their records. 3 Observe the loading Watch the vehicle being loaded onto the flatbed - ensure it is loaded safely and properly secured. 4 Confirm the destination Confirm the workshop address with the driver - avoid any confusion about the destination. 5 Get a reference number Ask for a job reference number or tracking number - so you can track the vehicle if needed. 6 Take photos during loading Take photos of the vehicle being loaded - additional evidence of condition during transport. After Collection 1 Confirm arrival time Confirm the expected arrival time at the workshop - so you can notify the workshop. 2 Keep the reference number Keep the job reference number handy - for tracking and any follow-up. 3 Contact the workshop Confirm the workshop is ready to receive the vehicle - avoid any delays at the drop-off. Supplier Checklist What to Ask the Recovery Supplier Before Booking A checklist of questions to protect yourself and avoid surprises. What type of recovery vehicle will you use? Confirm it's a flatbed - not a tow rope or A-frame. What's the estimated arrival time? Manage your expectations - how long will you wait? What's the total cost - any additional charges? Check for hidden charges - storage, mileage overrun, etc. What's the cancellation policy? If your plans change, can you cancel without penalty? Do you have insurance for transport damage? Confirm they have insurance - what's the claims process? Can I get a tracking number? So you can track the vehicle during transport. Do you take photos of the vehicle before loading? Many recovery companies do - this protects both parties. What happens if the workshop isn't ready? Is there a storage charge? What's the process? What should I do if there's an issue? Contact process - who do you speak to? Don't Assume What NOT to Ask or Assume Common misconceptions that can lead to problems. ❌ "Engines Market arranges the recovery" No - we connect you with recovery specialists. You arrange directly with the recovery supplier. ❌ "The recovery driver can fix my car" No - they are transport specialists, not mechanics. Recovery transports - repairs are separate. ⚠️ "My breakdown cover will cover this" Maybe - check your policy. Some cover recovery to a garage, some don't. ❌ "The driver will take the vehicle to a workshop of their choice" No - you choose the workshop. Confirm the destination with the driver. ❌ "I don't need to take photos - it's all fine" Wrong - always take photos. Photograph the vehicle before, during, and after transport. Real-World Validation What Recovery Specialists Say Insights drawn from interviews with UK recovery specialists. [EM-INTERVIEW] "We photographed a customer's vehicle before loading - and we photographed the vehicle on arrival. The workshop claimed there was damage to the bumper that 'must have happened during transport.' The photos proved the damage was there before we collected it. The workshop charged £20/day for storage - £60 extra. All arrangements are directly between you and the recovery supplier. We help you compare quotes and choose the right service. What type of recovery should I choose for engine failure? + Flatbed recovery is the only safe option for engine and gearbox failures. Tow ropes can damage the vehicle - especially automatics. Should I take photos before recovery? + Yes - always take clear photos of all four sides and the interior before the vehicle is collected. Also ask the recovery driver if they have taken photos. This protects you in case of transport damage. Can I arrange recovery to any workshop? + Yes - you choose the workshop. Confirm the address with the driver and ensure the workshop is ready to receive the vehicle. What if the workshop isn't ready when the vehicle arrives? + Some recovery companies charge storage fees if the workshop isn't ready. Always confirm the workshop is ready before booking recovery. Does my breakdown cover include recovery? + Some policies include recovery to a garage - check your policy. If not, you can arrange recovery through our network. What's the typical response time? + Standard booking: 24-48 hours. Emergency same-day recovery: usually available but at a premium (£100-£200 extra). Can I arrange recovery + engine replacement together? + Yes - many specialists offer combined recovery + engine replacement services. Get combined quotes → What if my vehicle is damaged during transport? + Recovery specialists have insurance for transport damage. Take photos before and during loading. If damage occurs, contact the recovery specialist immediately. sections.heading: Don't risk driving - get a flatbed recovery quote

blocks.text: You've seen the data - recovery costs, flatbed advice, and a clear checklist. Now get quotes from vetted UK recovery specialists. Free, no obligation, quotes in 30-60 minutes.
Based on real UK recovery specialist quotes · Engines Market is a comparison platform - we connect you with vetted recovery specialists, we do not provide recovery services.
Free · No obligation · 100+ vetted specialists · Flatbed recovery only

rows: No compression, no start, risk of further damage
Driving could destroy the engine completely

faqs.question: How much does vehicle recovery cost? +
faqs.answer: Local recovery (under 25 miles) £50-£150, regional (25-100 miles) £100-£300, national (100+ miles) £200-£600. Prices vary by distance and vehicle type. [EM-QUOTE]

faqs.question: Do Engines Market arrange recovery directly? +
faqs.answer: No - Engines Market connects you with vetted recovery specialists. All arrangements are directly between you and the recovery supplier. We help you compare quotes and choose the right service.

faqs.question: What type of recovery should I choose for engine failure? +
faqs.answer: Flatbed recovery is the only safe option for engine and gearbox failures. Tow ropes can damage the vehicle - especially automatics.

faqs.question: Should I take photos before recovery? +
faqs.answer: Yes - always take clear photos of all four sides and the interior before the vehicle is collected. Also ask the recovery driver if they have taken photos. This protects you in case of transport damage.

faqs.question: Can I arrange recovery to any workshop? +
faqs.answer: Yes - you choose the workshop. Confirm the address with the driver and ensure the workshop is ready to receive the vehicle.

faqs.question: What if the workshop isn't ready when the vehicle arrives? +
faqs.answer: Some recovery companies charge storage fees if the workshop isn't ready. Always confirm the workshop is ready before booking recovery.

faqs.question: Does my breakdown cover include recovery? +
faqs.answer: Some policies include recovery to a garage - check your policy. If not, you can arrange recovery through our network.

faqs.question: What's the typical response time? +
faqs.answer: Standard booking: 24-48 hours. Emergency same-day recovery: usually available but at a premium (£100-£200 extra).

faqs.question: Can I arrange recovery + engine replacement together? +
faqs.answer: Yes - many specialists offer combined recovery + engine replacement services. Get combined quotes →

faqs.question: What if my vehicle is damaged during transport? +
faqs.answer: Recovery specialists have insurance for transport damage. Take photos before and during loading. If damage occurs, contact the recovery specialist immediately.
